about: The install route: the arc CLI on the coding machine, then the pipeline machine, ending with a first PR the pipeline landed. probe.py reads it and reports, per stage, which criterion holds and which does not; SKILL.md walks it in order. Each stage names the machine it is judged on: `coding` (where the person writes code) or `pipeline` (the machine that runs the server suite); probe.py judges the stages of the machine it is told it runs on. Every stage is judged from the world (files, binaries, git, the board's answers) each time, so a stopped install resumes by probing again.

criteria.says: the directory is inside a git work tree
the machine is one getarc ships a binary for (macOS arm64, Linux x86_64)
python3 is 3.11+ (tomllib), so the TOML checks below can read config files
`arc` runs and prints a version
the installed arc has every verb this route uses (`arc <verb> --help` succeeds)

stages.title: LLM providers in tars
asks: Which model providers do you have access to (an API key, or a signed-in Claude Code / Codex / agy CLI)?

criteria.says: <tars home>/config.toml exists
it parses as TOML and has at least one [providers.<id>] with a known type
arc itself reads it and lists its provider ids (`arc init` in a throwaway repo — tars refuses an unknown key here)
every env-var credential a provider names is set in this shell, and every CLI provider's executable is on PATH

stages.title: arc init: .arc/config.toml [roles]
asks: Which tars provider reviews (critic) and which fixes (fixer)? The fixer should be a different model family.

criteria.says: .arc/config.toml exists
it has no [providers] section (arc refuses one)
every [roles] value names a provider id in tars, and a critic resolves (critic_l4 / critic / default)
fixer is written out (it never falls back to default)
fixer and critic are different model families
a claude_cli fixer has tools = "default"; a codex_cli fixer has sandbox = "workspace-write"
the fixer provider's agent CLI (claude / codex / agy) is on PATH
`arc rot --no-judge` exits 0 here (binary, repo and [review] exclude all read)
the repo has an origin remote (`arc submit` pushes to it, and it names the tenant)
`gh auth status` succeeds (`arc submit` opens the PR through gh)

stages.title: presubmit.toml: the checks before arc submit pushes
asks: Which commands must pass on your machine before a change is pushed (the build, the tests, a lint)? arc submit runs them, and arc fix tells the fixer to run them before it calls a finding fixed.
stages.verify: arc presubmit --target origin/<target> --base "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/<target>)"

criteria.says: presubmit.toml is at the repo root (arc submit and arc fix read it from the working tree)
presubmit.toml is committed on origin's default branch, so every branch carries it

stages.title: Merge gate: .github/workflows/merge.yml
asks: Which checks must pass before a PR lands on the target branch (build, tests, lint)?

criteria.says: .github/workflows/merge.yml exists
`arc workflow … --list` exits 0 for every job arc reads in the file
merge.yml is committed on origin's default branch: the merge machine reads it from the base of every change

stages.title: The arc-hold label on GitHub
asks: May I create the `arc-hold` label on the GitHub repo (and `arc-bypass`, if a review route will name it)?

criteria.says: the repo has the `arc-hold` label, which keeps a PR from landing

stages.title: The server suite and what the pipeline machine needs
asks: Which machine runs the pipeline: this one, or another (Linux x86_64 with systemd recommended)? Can this agent run commands there, or will you run them and paste the output?

criteria.says: every suite binary the pipeline runs (arc, arc-server, arc-review, arc-reviewer, arc-fixer, arc-web, arc-bridge) is on PATH and prints its version
git is 2.38 or newer (arc-server refuses to start on an older one)
`gh auth status` succeeds as the user the services run as (the merge server pushes and the review service reads labels through gh)
systemd keeps this user's services after logout and starts them at boot (`loginctl enable-linger`); a machine without systemd cannot

sources: docs/user-guide/install.md (The pipeline machine, The server suite)

stages.title: ~/.arc/machine.toml: [machine]
asks: Which IP address do the coding machines reach this machine at? Which directories hold the toolchains merge.yml runs (for `path`)?

criteria.says: arc-server reads ~/.arc/machine.toml (`arc-server tenant list` exits 0)
[machine] has an address and expose = true, so other machines reach the board; without it the board listens on 127.0.0.1 only

stages.title: arc-bridge and arc-web: the chat server and the board

criteria.says: arc-web answers GET /api/machine at the address `arc-server tenant url web` prints
arc-bridge answers GET /healthz at the address the board gives for it
arc-web.service and arc-bridge.service are enabled systemd user units, so they come back after a reboot

stages.title: Register the repo: a dedicated clone, a [[tenant]], its review routes
asks: Where should the clone only arc works in live (for example ~/<repo>-ci)? Which branch do PRs land on (default main)? Who reviews: the dummy reviewer (says LGTM to everything, no model) or a model reviewer (react)?

criteria.says: ~/.arc/machine.toml has a [[tenant]] with this repo's owner/name (`arc-server install <clone>` writes it)
the tenant has at least one [[tenant.review.route]]: with none, nobody reviews and nothing lands
a route to a model reviewer (basic / react) has a critic_l4 or default role in the clone's .arc/config.toml (or review.model_config) naming a provider in this machine's tars config
`arc-server tenant check <owner/name>` exits 0 and every line says ok or skip

stages.title: Start the repo's services: arc-server@, arc-review@, then restart arc-web

criteria.says: the board on this machine lists the tenant with its merge and review stores open (its services ran, and arc-web was restarted after)
arc-server@<owner>-<name>.service and arc-review@<owner>-<name>.service are enabled systemd user units

stages.title: This machine talks to the pipeline: ~/.arc/client.toml and the agent hooks
asks: What did `arc-server tenant url web` print on the pipeline machine? Which coding agent do you use (Claude Code, Codex CLI, agy)?

criteria.says: ~/.arc/client.toml names the board (`web = "http://<address>:<port>"`)
the board answers GET /api/machine from this machine
the board lists this repo (its origin's owner/name) as a tenant, with its merge and review stores open
the agent's settings run `arc bridge hook …`, so findings and each PR's outcome reach its session

stages.title: The first PR: arc submit, reviewed and landed by the pipeline
asks: May I run `arc submit` on a feature branch? It pushes the branch and opens a PR.

criteria.says: the board's merge record for this repo counts at least one landed PR

stages.title: Deploy: [release] in the tenant clone + .arc/delivery.toml
asks: Does this repo deploy from the pipeline machine? If so, which workflow job is the deploy?

criteria.says: [release] in the tenant clone's .arc/config.toml names a workflow (and job); the deploy runs in that clone
`arc workflow <file> --job <job> --list` exits 0 (without --job when [release] names none)
`arc workflow <file> --job <job> --list` names a concurrency group the job holds, its own or the file-wide one
.arc/delivery.toml has exactly one [builds.*] naming the same workflow and job
